competencies.text: Investigate how pressure is transmitted in fluids.
Explain how cross-sectional area affects output force. Analyze electricity consumption data and propose energy-efficient practices.

days.title: Pascal's Principle & Fluid Pressure
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain Pascal's Principle, describe how pressure transmits through fluids, and analyze how changing the cross-sectional area affects the output force in hydraulic systems.

💧 What Is Pressure?

Pressure is the force applied per unit area:

Pressure (P) = Force (F) ÷ Area (A)
Unit: Pascal (Pa) = 1 Newton per square meter

This is why a sharp knife cuts better than a dull one — the same force on a smaller area creates greater pressure.

🔬 Pascal's Principle

Pascal's Principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally to every part of the fluid and to the walls of the container.

This means: if you push down on one side of a hydraulic system, the pressure you create is felt everywhere in the fluid — and it can be used to move a much larger piston on the other side.

⚙️ How a Hydraulic System Works

A hydraulic system has two pistons connected by a fluid-filled tube:

ComponentRole
Small piston (input)You apply a small force over a small area → creates pressure
FluidTransmits that pressure throughout the system
Large piston (output)Same pressure over a larger area → produces a much larger output force

📐 The Hydraulic Equation

F₁ ÷ A₁ = F₂ ÷ A₂

Where:
F₁ = input force, A₁ = input area
F₂ = output force, A₂ = output area

Key insight: The pressure is the same on both sides, so a bigger area produces a bigger force. This is called force multiplication.

🛠️ Real-Life Applications

  • Car brakes: Pressing the brake pedal (small piston) multiplies force to stop a heavy vehicle.
  • Hydraulic jacks: Lift cars with just a small effort on the handle.
  • Excavators: Move heavy arms and buckets with precision.
  • Dentist chairs: Raise and lower patients smoothly.
  • Barangay water pumps: Use fluid pressure to lift water from deep wells.

⚡ Energy Management — Why It Matters

Hydraulic and other mechanical systems run on energy. In the Philippines, most electricity comes from coal, natural gas, and geothermal plants. Using energy efficiently:

  • Saves money on electric bills.
  • Reduces carbon emissions.
  • Reduces strain on the national grid.

Look at your own Meralco (or local utility) bill — the kilowatt-hour (kWh) is the unit of electrical energy consumed. Reducing kWh = saving money.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why does a hydraulic jack lift a car with little effort? (Answer: pressure is transmitted through fluid and multiplies output force via larger piston area)
  • If F₁ = 50 N on A₁ = 0.01 m², what is the pressure? (Answer: 5000 Pa)
  • If that same pressure acts on A₂ = 0.5 m², what is F₂? (Answer: 2500 N)

days.title: Match Game — Hydraulic Systems
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each hydraulic concept or device to its correct description or example. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Force divided by area (measured in Pascals)
Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally throughout
You apply small force over a small area
Same pressure over a larger area = greater output force
Lifts a car using force multiplication
Small pedal press → large braking force
Unit of electrical energy on your bill
Using less energy to do the same work

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Energy Consumption
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🚗 You press the brake pedal of a car with a force of 40 N. The pedal piston has an area of 0.002 m². What pressure is created in the brake fluid?
💧 A hydraulic jack has an input piston of area 0.005 m² and an output piston of area 0.25 m². If you apply 100 N on the input, what is the output force?
🏠 Your family's electric bill increased by ₱800 this month. Which action BEST reduces future electricity consumption?

choices.label: B) Unplugging appliances when not in use and switching to LED bulbs
D) Leaving lights on all night

scenario.text: 🏗️ An excavator uses hydraulics to move its heavy metal arm. Why is a fluid used instead of a solid rod?

choices.label: A) Fluids are cheaper than metal rods.
B) Fluids transmit pressure equally in all directions and can be controlled precisely.
D) Fluids create energy out of nothing.

scenario.text: 🌡️ A household appliance uses 1,500 W and runs 4 hours per day. How much energy does it consume per day in kWh?

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Energy Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Energy Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Pascal's Principle applies to which state of matter?
In a hydraulic system, if the output piston has a LARGER area than the input piston, what happens to the output force?
What is the unit of pressure in the SI system?
Which of the following is NOT a practical application of hydraulics?
A 100 W light bulb runs for 10 hours per day. How many kWh does it consume per day?
Which practice BEST improves household energy efficiency?

choices.label: A) Running appliances at peak hours
B) Using incandescent bulbs instead of LED
C) Setting aircon to 24–26°C and cleaning filters regularly
D) Leaving the refrigerator door open
